independent_reviews.text:
# Independent described-by patch review

Reviewed 2026-11-07 against canonical clean HEAD `87d381f56b545081bfb87b1d5f1a1e1e9941d2eb`; patch SHA-256 `1e773596c989c36e376615c74fcb86ab220169d45d3cfefc2b46489a485aee70`. The retained `reviewed.patch` is byte-identical. `git apply --check` succeeds. Preimages retained here: `form-field.preimage.ts` SHA-256 `ea2bcd2a85cb1511cfa57a7d68d2edd45757ecd703df0ebfa0d613e3f4b79ccd` (Git blob `dda4b47f4b06f5f354f23b90a799794c5c47b02c`); `input-spec.preimage.ts` SHA-256 `025f4fa2579ce0d93e95dc7cfe266081d3d0d771bb31c9ccc71ff8970c478eae` (blob `92f54815f50962f0038fd98aa5880f4bdd685ce7`). The external candidate's exact diff hashes to the reviewed patch; postimages hash to `a9ef781d59ac8bf11374ad0cc903b379cbfd8b8e19643c06a8e2df0808a12927` and `39a618496b90a1d860e05ee54a611f47274d7045122380edd26f6ee9dcec716a` respectively. No canonical edits or remote actions.

## Assessment

The production change is a narrow, reasonable repair of the confirmed stale description case. Material 16.2.14 reference `src/material/legacy-form-field/form-field.ts` lines 337–342 calls validation, description synchronization and markForCheck for every state notification. The candidate's filtered pairwise subscription only reacts to error state or user description changes; it misses changed IDs on existing hint/error objects. The patch restores the reference ordering on the already-owned state subscription and removes the redundant filtered subscriber. Initial synchronization remains explicit. No template, CSS, Sass or selector changes are present.

The existing sync logic collects user IDs and current hint/error IDs, then retains externally assigned IDs except IDs last assigned by the form field. Installed MatInput reads current DOM IDs and writes the combined list. The proposed assertion checks exactly one current ID, removal of the old ID, and preservation of a separate external ID for each visible hint and error. In the patch the ID bindings are rendered before the discriminating state emissions; error visibility is explicitly established. Actual execution of this repository spec is still needed: `fixture.detectChanges()` and the AOT browser fixture use different notification/change-detection sequences, and the former has not been executed at this review cutoff. Do not claim the added regression passes or discriminates until run against baseline and fix.

On control replacement, `_initializeControl` unsubscribes the previous `_stateChanges` before subscribing to the new control; destruction unsubscribes it. Deleting the second subscription removes its teardown with it. This is sound by source inspection; neither replacement nor destruction has a targeted runtime regression in this patch or the provided browser fixture. Those lifecycle checks remain open. `_describedByIds` persistence across replacement predates this change and was not broadly requalified here.

Every state event now writes the description attribute and scans the hints/errors, increasing DOM work compared with the filtered pipeline; this restores the original behavior, and no perf measurement was performed. Installed MatInput's `setDescribedByIds` performs DOM reads/writes without notifying state. A custom control that synchronously emits `stateChanges` from `setDescribedByIds` could recurse; the reference also synchronizes in the notification callback, but this risk was not runtime tested and no general safety claim is made.

## Browser evidence and identity

Reviewed owner addendum `../dom-addendum.md` SHA-256 `d0e937888b6888e621ee274b0c3fb975025215b5e1a3bb0cc0f0a114d2feea14` and runtime manifest `../dom-manifest.json` SHA-256 `199625649f535833cd7071a1b3b45e51208024866d71eea63b8d3fdeb3cb56c1`. Independently rehashed both tarballs and all 512 regular members per tarball against their extracted counterparts and the manifest: no mismatches. Tar hashes: baseline `2828f71233d13791de86971a6d18bdc35d88d8285a9c0ed30ad624a8dff9fbe1`, fixed `fbea62412013d2915c27801117dfda44ff550a0c392d599b4846c46719dd6a8c`. Both esbuild metafiles identify the extracted artifact's form-field and input modules; fixture links partially compiled Angular code and uses strict AOT compilation. Source applies no test-only private override.

Raw command logs show baseline probe exit 1, fixed exit 0, and results show Chrome 149 with old IDs remaining on baseline and new IDs plus external IDs on fix. The fixture marks the views, sends one state notification, ticks to render the new IDs, then sends a second notification; unchanged error/user-description fields make the second notification discriminate the filter. This is credible narrow packed-artifact behavioral evidence, not proof that IDs update without a subsequent state notification. The baseline and fixed packs are based on a synthetic common-barrel source commit, not a new pack of canonical HEAD; the relevant preimage matches canonical and the fixed external source diff exactly matches the reviewed patch. I inspected the retained evidence and independently checked identities; I did not execute the browser or product tests.

This review neither establishes full source/audit coverage nor G11 or release qualification. Browser, peer version, error-state setup, and lifecycle limitations in the addendum apply; cross-version behavior, SSR, zoneless, full historical family and broader regression checks are unexecuted here. Final integration should run the new repository regression and affected family tests on the actual integrated candidate and perform the outstanding lifecycle check.

# Independent maintained-runner evidence review

This addendum supplements `report.md` SHA-256 `5edc8ec17512264c563073aa66e46be2950eec58f5d7d64b2b8fa84bd2e7f2db`. It supersedes only that report's statement that the added repository spec had not been run.

Reviewed owner `../runner-addendum.md` SHA-256 `6e58f6ffd7d531d11da6833c9f6a2e8ec4ce52c40fb0ed40f65261efab087b09`; independently rehashed raw JSON baseline `f5588eee4065f37116de416a2c78c0803589faaa6a1bcd0a0ffd28ee14dd03e7`, fixed `f9c46c995a52355c8adb62c9996e609a3822bc7a3eb604696d2e5f97a4fa0331`, and logs `eded1594e3f263760cc40c8afe00595876119d961bbf81455b667361551cd0b4` and `52c14517120a65bcbbefd6147bfd86a60a30c9f65360e32886879817f559cd2a`. Each report lists 152 executed cases, with no skips. The specific added case appears once in each: baseline fails with both stale hint and stale error expectations; fixed succeeds. Baseline has one failure record, fixed none; the Karma logs corroborate totals and show normal `expectFail=false`, so the retained records show no suppressed failure. This is a targeted review of the retained evidence and runner paths, not an exhaustive runner integrity audit.

The external runner tree is detached at `87d381f56b545081bfb87b1d5f1a1e1e9941d2eb`, with only the two reviewed files modified. Both postimage SHA-256 values match the earlier independent review. The byte-different generated diff has only abbreviated Git index hashes differing; reviewed patch remains `1e773596c989c36e376615c74fcb86ab220169d45d3cfefc2b46489a485aee70`. The fixed bundle SHA-256 is `239f5b7a4c5876e95a3270df07a182838b56767b831bf274457732414e0d064e`; baseline bundle was overwritten. Source and log inspection shows the maintained wrapper building in artifact mode, specifying each external package root, then executing the Karma/Jasmine browser test, with normal failure handling. The alias resolves package exports to the supplied root; artifact-mode guards prohibit ordinary workspace component/module and dist imports, while permitting specs and helper files. The runner uses the 87d source and linked canonical dependencies. Its sandboxed Chrome launcher has no sandbox-disabling flag; sandbox enforcement itself was not independently measured in this run.

The JSON's `artifact_sha256` field is null: direct package-root invocation does not bind it itself. Package-root paths agree with the previously independently checked extraction manifest, whose 512 files per tarball were byte-compared to their respective tarball, and the two tarball hashes are recorded in the earlier report. This binding relies on the retained files and a quiescent workspace between verification and execution; it is not a transactional artifact receipt. Baseline and fixed tarballs are the earlier synthetic common-barrel packs, not a fresh pack of canonical HEAD. The earlier independent AOT packed-browser observation and this maintained runner provide complementary evidence of the same bounded regression.

The new repository test is therefore observed failing against baseline and passing against the fixed packed candidate; the fixed input family reports 152/152. Control replacement/destroy remains source-reviewed only, with no targeted runtime test. No broader family suite, other peer line/browser, zoneless, SSR, audit or release qualification follows. I did not rerun the browser or modify canonical source.

aot_dom_addendum.text:
# Described-by DOM reproduction and proposed patch

This addendum does not alter `report.md`, `inventory.json`, the prior source diffs, or the original finding record. The finding is now reproduced in a real browser for the specific sequence below. The patch remains a proposal for independent review; canonical was not edited.

## Result

A strict-template, `skipLibCheck:false`, AOT consumer compiled and linked the actual extracted packed package, then ran in sandbox-enabled Chrome/149.0.7827.0 using the existing repository browser helper and pinned Chrome binary SHA-256 `3a0b4b909e867cbd845162be0b67343c0d6bb03dbac8f2d410eec8fcc8913fe9`. Node was 24.21.0, Python 3.14.8, installed Angular/CDK/Material 22.1.7. Browser sandbox enabled follows the retained same-binary/helper smoke record, not a separate sandbox measurement in this fixture.

| Packed subject | Hint after notification | Error after notification | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline `2828f71233d13791de86971a6d18bdc35d88d8285a9c0ed30ad624a8dff9fbe1` | `old-hint external-hint` | `old-error external-error` | fail (probe exit 1) |
| Fresh fix `fbea62412013d2915c27801117dfda44ff550a0c392d599b4846c46719dd6a8c` | `new-hint external-hint` | `new-error external-error` | pass (probe exit 0) |

For both, the preceding recorded snapshot confirms rendered hint/error IDs already read `new-hint`/`new-error` before the final notification, and unchanged control fields are `[false,null]` and `[true,null]` for error state and userAriaDescribedBy, respectively. The initial snapshot confirms both old IDs and outside IDs are present. A first public `stateChanges.next()` marks the OnPush views so the bound IDs render; after that render, the second public state notification is the discriminating check. It does not establish a guarantee that description IDs update immediately without a subsequent state notification. The test sets the public input error state to display an error and writes the outside described-by IDs to the native elements as an external DOM describer would; it does not mutate private implementation or inject candidate source into the test. No test changes the hint/error QueryList membership during the check. The source analysis in the original report establishes why no other query/hintLabel path updates these IDs in this scenario.

Raw retained observations: `baseline-dom-v4/result.json` SHA-256 `438d9a874c226f8ef7504cbb4f8549036be240960fd289e7652af8fea4acb9fb`, commands `f4acdbed184d4cdea4c2d086d873cc576f9cf72ebbc4df21e3a70a17314eac4d`; `fixed-dom-v2/result.json` SHA-256 `82106928ac9071ce3726ada66b61a80f6bcfba70da4360cda7ccba3b095812e4`, commands `48b45c5d9ccdf7608f8c1fe4d12adde94de228016ae350e75f9ad88d6f1b477e`. Commands record tar extraction, ngc, linking/bundling, browser and exit status. Both esbuild metafiles list the three owned modules exclusively under `../artifact/package/fesm2022/` (core, form field, input), not workspace library sources. Baseline/fixed metafile SHA-256 values are `810d1335bd104861f6110af7b53cfe3edc86de107a89a3e05fac955a5e55d74c` / `0a0e58d0d26ba18c4ff19065463e68362311d97dc888b8ab22110d7c0825f3d6`.

## Source and fixture identity

The baseline is the synthetic isolated common-barrel pack described in `compatibility/rc/parent-main-common-module-sandboxed-observation-v1.json`, not a pack of current canonical HEAD. Fresh fix pack built from an external copy of its synthetic source commit `8d268a3d456a606a8363cc546642e2e0f68f452d` with a dirty product + spec patch, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.4.2 and npm 11.19.0; see `fixed-pack-v1.log` and `fixed-pack-v1/pack-meta.json`. Baseline source `form-field.ts` SHA-256 is `ea2bcd2a85cb1511cfa57a7d68d2edd45757ecd703df0ebfa0d613e3f4b79ccd` (also matches reviewed `19ee63433` and the synthetic pack source); fixed file `a9ef781d59ac8bf11374ad0cc903b379cbfd8b8e19643c06a8e2df0808a12927`. Fixed spec SHA-256 `39a618496b90a1d860e05ee54a611f47274d7045122380edd26f6ee9dcec716a`.

The proposed patch `described-by-fix.patch` SHA-256 `1e773596c989c36e376615c74fcb86ab220169d45d3cfefc2b46489a485aee70` restores description synchronization in the existing state subscription, retains its explicit replacement/destroy unsubscription and removes the separate filtered subscription. It also adds a source regression case covering dynamically bound hint and error IDs and external IDs. It changes no HTML, CSS or SCSS. The fixture independently verifies the behavior against the actual package, but the new repository spec itself has **not** been executed; its adaptation/compilation and target-family result remain required at integration. In particular, fixture lifecycle differs from the proposed spec's explicit `fixture.detectChanges()` sequence. Control swaps, cleanup, custom controls whose `setDescribedByIds` emits synchronously, and broader suite regressions remain to be tested/reviewed.

Fixture SHA-256: `main.ts` `d852e49e65d51c17ee88c0b29e841ff27818512eeb0f63173051e79348758b4d`; `probe.mjs` `6ee7a163c4402ad461078ecf79a9b28c284ac7a979e1893ce698c7e2b3475f0f`; `run.mjs` `dd92687d7810eac6162126ea6c6b8eb263f17a38f76cea8afe522c0e1d35f20a`; `build.mjs` `eea38d2b39e536615d1172f85915f2cbad520573d410fbf8785b0a3b22b3c02d`; `tsconfig.json` `8bb67cce342fbe67fd6b619322aa78541e9e29c9d33573629563319e79e46f49`; `index.html` `6ebc48082b355b6dd1c7dfd85abe69a68b7545ee460e69c3fdf0ddf630953fa7`. `baseline-dom-v1` and `v2` were intermediate attempts before correcting change detection; `v3` is the first discriminating baseline and v4 adds explicit snapshot/state predicates. `fixed-dom-v1` predates those added predicates; v2 uses the same fixture as v4.

No current HEAD package, other browser, zoneless mode, 21.x peer, SSR, style equality, full historical family or release gate is claimed. Any integration intentionally changes source-bound evidence; this work does not re-stamp it.

# Maintained historical runner check

At external detached source commit `87d381f56b545081bfb87b1d5f1a1e1e9941d2eb`, applied unchanged `described-by-fix.patch` SHA-256 `1e773596c989c36e376615c74fcb86ab220169d45d3cfefc2b46489a485aee70`; the two resulting files hash to `a9ef781d59ac8bf11374ad0cc903b379cbfd8b8e19643c06a8e2df0808a12927` (product) and `39a618496b90a1d860e05ee54a611f47274d7045122380edd26f6ee9dcec716a` (spec), identical to the fix candidate. `runner-applied.patch` differs bytewise only in Git's abbreviated `index` hash lengths (SHA-256 `88b39207615c3beb632dc66ebec7247080dd6122424134aaaddd9be564b549e3`). Node modules symlink points to canonical peer dependencies; the only tracked source changes in the detached tree are the two patch files.

Ran `node scripts/run-legacy-tests.mjs` with `LEGACY_SPEC_FAMILY=input`, `LEGACY_SUBJECT_MODE=artifact`, unique absolute `LEGACY_RESULTS_PATH`, and `LEGACY_PACKAGE_ROOT` set first to `baseline-dom-v4/artifact/package`, then `fixed-dom-v2/artifact/package`. `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_PATH` and `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` were unset; PATH began Node 24.21.0 and Python 3.14.7; `CHROME_BIN` was `/nix/store/xwgjkr6hdj8600wf25pnrb0hsx352qr2-playwright-chromium/chrome-linux/chrome`, SHA-256 `3a0b4b909e867cbd845162be0b67343c0d6bb03dbac8f2d410eec8fcc8913fe9`. The Karma launcher uses ChromeHeadlessSandboxed, no sandbox-disabling flags; independent same-binary sandbox smoke is referenced in the DOM addendum, not directly measured by these runs. No retries were made.

Baseline: 152 executed, 151 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped. The sole failed case was `MatInput without forms > updates descriptions when existing hint and error IDs change on a state notification`, with both old hint and error description values remaining; raw `runner-baseline-v1.json` SHA-256 `f5588eee4065f37116de416a2c78c0803589faaa6a1bcd0a0ffd28ee14dd03e7`, log `eded1594e3f263760cc40c8afe00595876119d961bbf81455b667361551cd0b4`. Runner result `artifact_sha256` is null because this direct invocation supplied package roots, not `LEGACY_ARTIFACT_SHA256`; the byte-level extraction-to-tar verification and independent tar hashes are preserved in `dom-manifest.json`, rather than implied by that field.

Build alias logic resolves legacy package subpaths against `LEGACY_PACKAGE_ROOT` and refuses component/module workspace imports in artifact mode. The fixed run's generated bundle SHA-256 `239f5b7a4c5876e95a3270df07a182838b56767b831bf274457732414e0d064e`, source map `9dd3f0f31ddc645b14ea191949f0234da20c6c84d1656440e837f7e9a8b60790`, and bundled-spec roster `fc4c0ce5d205bdc6887d570312be749911372f38c1476768e2fb05ce89fe29ac` remain under `runner-source-v1/testing/legacy-runner/out/`; those paths are generated output for the *fixed* run only, baseline bundle was overwritten by the runner. Source-map names are provenance metadata and not independent proof of resolution. `scripts/run-legacy-tests.mjs` SHA-256 `b5e4072a685bddb7c738f0c3d9fe830ebf4ae06a499bf4a5783aab7354bd2fbc`; `testing/legacy-runner/build.mjs` `d2ad861fa584e7d0ba57aab60101cef46dfe2be5828f0f3df1dc8cd0e3bebb94`; `adapt-spec.mjs` `668f2a08a004a9ba0b97a1738df051dcb9f81eb50a98672155c83c842b0cc6b3`; Karma config `fd9b5c1e77c928f4cb1b5e41be908ffa57e9ce4cf4570c2dfcbe403fac6be447`.

This is a single artifact-bound input family observation, not a full suite, fresh canonical pack, acceptance gate, 21.x, cross-browser, zoneless, or style compatibility result.
